blocks.title: Variable
blocks.text: A variable works as a storage container in the computer's memory, holding data that can be retrieved and changed later in the program. Its value can change while the program runs, which is why it is called a variable.

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
age = 71
print("Quaid-i-Azam lived for", age, "years")
age = 60
print("Allama Iqbal lived for", age, "years")
Here the variable age is given different values to show the ages of Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah and Allama Iqbal, which are printed as part of the output.

Comments are lines that the Python interpreter does not run; they give explanations or notes about the code. A single-line comment starts with #, and a multi-line comment can be written between triple quotes at the beginning and the end.

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
# This is a single-line comment
print("K2 is the second-highest mountain in the world")
"""
This is a multi-line comment.
It can span multiple lines.
"""
print("Edhi Foundation operates the world's largest volunteer ambulance network.")
